Conditional facility-case bootstrap for a fitted allocation

Source: R/07-allocation_bootstrap.R
bootstrap_allocation.Rd

This experimental operation runs separately from fitting. It resamples facility observation multiplicities, retaining every physical facility and its supply in the allocation network. Need, travel, capacity and included-network inputs remain fixed. Facility independence is a caller-declared working assumption.

Usage

bootstrap_allocation(
  model,
  fit,
  observation,
  scenario = NULL,
  seed,
  checkpoint = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A checked static CLM from clm_allocation() with a fitted outside mass (fit_v0 = TRUE), a decay kernel that is smooth in sigma (built in, or declared with decay_kernel() and smooth = TRUE), and known travel on its retained demand support. The supply elasticity beta may be fixed or fitted; kappa and a fixed beta may be any positive values. It can instead be a result of spax() that fitted such a model to facility totals: the result supplies its bound model and its fit, so leave fit out and give observation by name. A Huff model, a fit to flows and an evaluated result are refused as for the model and fit given separately.

fit

A matching multistart fit of complete whole facility counts using the unweighted built-in Poisson objective. Fractional or partial observations, flow targets, fits with observed outside counts (flow_outside, utilization_outside: the facility-case bootstrap is defined for facility totals without outside counts) and custom objectives are outside this method. Not given when model is a result of spax().

observation

Named list declaring nonblank event, period (including an explicit unresolved reference date), and sampling="independent_facilities". Non-overlapping registration alone does not establish independence.

scenario

Optional checked CLM whose prepared system changes supply only. Every draw evaluates baseline and scenario together at the same parameters.

seed

Required nonnegative integer; attempt b uses seed+b. The caller's RNG state and RNG kind are restored, including when interrupted.

checkpoint

Optional RDS file in an existing directory. Completed attempts are saved atomically and resumed after exact input/settings/version checks. Completed failures are never retried; incomplete runs retain actual counts.

Value

An ae_allocation_bootstrap with compact draws, multiplicities, all start diagnostics, assumptions, failure reasons and conditional percentile intervals for each fitted parameter (sigma, v0 and, when fitted, beta), regional contact and optional paired change in modeled contacts. Regional attributed capacity per need is a fixed-input identity without an interval: it includes supply with at least one known finite edge on retained demand support. Unsupported positive supply is disclosed in capacity_support; total supplied capacity can exceed attributed capacity. For any model other than built-in Gaussian decay with fitted sigma and v0 and kappa and beta equal to 1, the result also has a coverage_note saying that coverage was evaluated for that case and not studied separately for the model; it is printed with the result. Scientific refusals are inspectable results; invalid inputs error.

Details

The model is a static CLM with a fitted outside mass (outside = "fit" in spec_clm(), or fit_v0 = TRUE in clm_allocation()) and a decay kernel that is smooth in sigma: the Gaussian, exponential or power kernel, or a kernel declared with decay_kernel() (not with smooth = FALSE). The supply elasticity beta may be fixed or fitted. Every fitted parameter gets its own interval.

Exactly 399 attempts use the starts and positive bounds of the original fit (given, or found by the default search of fit_allocation()), with fixed numerical controls. Failed attempts are retained without replacement. Successful inner boundary estimates remain in the distribution. Original mean boundaries, local rank deficiency (fewer identified directions than fitted parameters) or insufficient fit precision, including a score that cannot be computed, refuse intervals; percentile intervals require a complete run of 399 attempts and at least 380 finite successful values per quantity. Incomplete results retain their point estimates and diagnostics but withhold intervals. Coverage was evaluated for Gaussian decay with fitted sigma and v0, in generated 80-origin/40-facility designs under tested fixed-input laws; other kernels and a fitted beta use the same procedure without a separate coverage study. Coverage validation is not a universal guarantee of exact 95 percent coverage or validation of an application's observation law.

A facility with positive supply, a known finite travel time on retained demand support and a modeled mean of exactly zero is treated as nonregular, so the original fit is refused and no intervals are available. This happens when the kernel is exactly zero at every finite travel time of such a facility, as a cutoff or bisquare kernel can be beyond its range, and also when Gaussian weights underflow to zero.

See also

Other allocation steps: calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_allocation(), clm_allocation(), compare_allocations(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), huff_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()
